articles.excerpt: Rescuers have recovered two bodies from the site of an avalanche that struck a climbing group camping in the Nepalese part of the Himalayas.Around a dozen people are still thought to be missing after a sheet of snow fell on the base camp of Himlung Himal peak on Manang district on Sunday morning.The group of Nepalese nationals, including climbers and support staff, had been sent ahead of foreign climbers to prepare the camp and fix ropes.Forecasts showed there was heavy snowfall around the 7,126m (23,380ft) peak in recent days, which lies on Nepal's border with Tibet.Poor weather has hampered rescue efforts, with helicopters and rescue teams initially unable to reach the site.Bibhuti Chand Thakur, of Himalaya Holidays Trekking, told news agency AFP that at least eight members of his expedition team had been reported missing. The exact number of climbers still unaccounted for remains unclear.A rescue team consisting of experienced mountaineers was rushed from the Nepalese capital, Kathmandu, via helicopter.

articles.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead
articles.excerpt: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Gunmen torched vehicles as they fled the scene of a mass shooting at bar near Johannesburg BySean Seddon and Thuthuka ZondiReporting fromJohannesburgTwenty-seven people have been killed in two mass shootings hours apart in South Africa, the latest gun violence to hit the country.Seventeen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar close to Johannesburg on Saturday evening, with 15 more injured.In a separate shooting in the early hours of Sunday morning, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town and a further 11 were injured.South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world and has struggled to contain gang-related gun violence in recent years. Police have not given a definitive motive for either of the latest attacks.In Johannesburg, gunmen opened fire on customers outside the bar before continuing the attack inside and torching two vehicles before fleeing.Police said thirteen men and four women were killed.Gauteng Police Commissioner Lt Gen Tommy Mthombeni said people from Ethiopia and Lesotho were among those caught up in the shooting, but that the vast majority were South African.He also said police believed the motive behind the shooting was robbery, as personal belongings had been taken, but that they could not rule out turf wars between illegal mining groups.Image caption, In Johannesburg, gunmen torched two vehicles after opened fire on customers at a bar.Mining without permission in abandoned shafts or dump sites is a persistent problem in South Africa, causing numerous deaths from unsafe conditions.

articles.title: Four killed in helicopter crash near Montreal
articles.excerpt: Four people have died after a helicopter crashed in a small town 50km (31 miles) from Montreal, Quebec's provincial police have told the BBC.Emergency services were called to Sainte-Brigide-d'Iberville shortly after 14:30 local time (18:30 GMT) on Saturday afternoon, where they found the aircraft on fire and declared its occupants dead at the scene.The victims have not yet been identified but the aircraft appeared to be a private helicopter, Sgt Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said.An investigation into the crash is being led by the Major Crime Unit of the Sûreté du Québec, working alongside crime scene technicians as well as investigators from the Transportation Safety Board of Canada.The crash site is located near the Rang des Écossais road off Highway 10, according to Bilodeau.Police were notified of a helicopter in distress that may have crashed and caught fire in an emergency call.An hour after the call, the fire at the site had been brought under control, though officials were still working at the crash site just before 22:00 local time.The victims have not yet been identified and Bilodeau said this process may "take a few days."

articles.title: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
articles.excerpt: Venezuelan authorities have released a slew of political prisoners, human rights groups say, days after the nation's interim leader met US President Donald Trump in New York.Among those released in the early hours of Saturday morning was Wilder Vasquez, who was handed a five-year sentence in 2018 over claims he was plotting to kill former President Nicolás Maduro.Opposition figures have renewed calls for free elections after interim President Delcy Rodriguez held talks with Trump, who captured Maduro earlier this year, at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday.Her administration previously released hundreds of prisoners as part of a reconciliation effort following Maduro's seizure.However, these releases slowed to a trickle in April after Rodriguez said the scheme was "coming to an end".Venezuela's government has not made any statement concerning the latest releases, nor has it indicated whether they were the result of her conversation with the US president.Gonzalo Himiob, vice-president of rights group Foro Penal, said "a significant number" of political prisoners had been released on Saturday morning from several of Venezuela's detention centres.Venezuelan Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, a minister closely associated with Maduro's authoritarian rule, called the interim president's meeting with Trump "a great triumph of the diplomacy of peace".But opposition voices expressed their disapproval over the meeting, viewing it as a snub of their calls – that the US has previously endorsed – for swift elections.Pedro Mario Burelli, a former Venezuelan state oil company executive and opposition commentator, called the two world leaders "the shameless puppet and her unscrupulous and undignified puppet-master", adding: "Little has changed in Venezuela under Washington's clumsy and selective oversight."Venezuela's last elections, held in 2024, in which Maduro was declared the winner, were widely disputed as rigged.

articles.title: Switzerland rejects stricter interpretation of its neutrality
articles.excerpt: Voters in Switzerland have overwhelmingly rejected a stricter interpretation of the country's tradition of diplomatic neutrality.More than 70% of Swiss voters rejected proposals that would have prevented the European nation from imposing sanctions without UN approval, official results showed.The move would have also prevented Switzerland from pursuing closer ties with the Nato military alliance.Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine has reopened the debate around Switzerland's centuries-old non-alignment.Moscow openly backed the initiative, which was supported by the right-wing Swiss People's Party (SVP) and opposed by the federal government and all other major parties.Lukas Golder, co-director of research institute Gfs.bern told Swiss public broadcaster SRF that Swiss voters had not rejected embracing its neutrality but that the vote showed Switzerland was in favour of sanctions against Russia."People have a clear idea of what Switzerland's neutrality is supposed to achieve," he said.Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis said during a recent televised debate that "neutrality has always been applied with a degree of flexibility".While Switzerland had no plans to lift a ban on selling arms to countries in conflict, including Ukraine, he stressed that "neutrality does not mean indifference".He added that Switzerland would "not look away when we see violations of the very international rules that allow us to live in peace".Switzerland was internationally recognised in 1815 when the country was granted "eternal neutrality" at the Congress of Vienna, during a period of war and upheaval in Europe.This neutrality was legally defined by the Hague Convention of 1907, which forbade Switzerland supplying weapons to countries at war. It previously rejected a request from Germany for ammunition for tanks being sent to Kyiv.Switzerland remained neutral through World War Two.

articles.title: Iranian minister says only negotiation can end conflict after Trump rejects Hormuz deal
articles.excerpt: Only a "negotiated solution" can end the conflict between the US and Iran, Tehran's foreign minister has said, after President Donald Trump publicly rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.Trump told reporters at the White House that Iran's proposal was not "acceptable" and that Tehran wanted to make a deal to open the strait to commercial shipping within seven days because "they're losing so badly".In a post on Telegram, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi acknowledged Trump's rejection, but said Iran would wait for a "definitive" official US response.He said the president had made contradictory statements in the past.Araghchi said the conditions to open the strait were the same that had been included in a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the US and Iran that was signed in June.Iran said it had raised reopening the strait and ending hostilities during negotiations on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this past week.The vital waterway through which around a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows has been effectively closed since the outbreak of war in February."I'm rejecting their deal," Trump said on Saturday, adding that the US already had "total control" of the strait, with "massive amounts of oil" passing through it, causing massive rises in global oil prices and steep fuel cost increases for consumers.Araghchi wrote on Telegram that Trump "has made many good statements, as well as many contradictory ones, which unfortunately we hear frequently".He continued: "We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them."Separately, Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, who travelled to New York for the UN general assembly, told the BBC's US news partner CBS that "distrust created by this war needs to be overcome" in order for talks to be successful.

articles.title: Pope says 'scourge' of abuse must be rooted out as he visits Lourdes
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo has called on French bishops to root out the "scourge" of sexual abuse in the Roman Catholic church, urging them to "maintain the greatest vigilance".The Pope delivered the message to bishops during a private meeting at the Sanctuary of Our Holy Lady of Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, on the third day of his four-day official visit to France.A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 people as children in France over 70 years.The Pope said Mass in front of thousands of worshippers in Lourdes before later meeting survivors of abuse.The Pope told the bishops: "You have faced with determination the painful scourge of abuse of minors committed by members of the clergy or within an ecclesial context."It is important to persevere along the path you have begun, maintaining the greatest vigilance."The gathering of senior church leaders was held behind closed doors and the remarks were later released to reporters.Leo then met with seven survivors of abuse by the French clergy.The Pope "thanked them for their painful testimony and reaffirmed his commitment to ensuring that the harm they experienced is not repeated for others", the Vatican said in a statement."It was extraordinary," said survivor Jean-Marie Delbos at a news conference following the encounter with the pontiff. He said Leo listened and was informed of their cases.

articles.title: One dead as nor'easter storm pummels New York and New Jersey
articles.excerpt: Figure caption, Watch: Huge waves pummel northeast US as storm barrels throughByKwasi Gyamfi AsieduUpdated 51 minutes agoTens of millions of people across the north-eastern US have found themselves in the path of a powerful weekend storm bringing coastal flooding, power cuts, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.The so-called nor'easter brought "dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston on Saturday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said. States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, both of which faced a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds were forecast from Virginia to Maine.In Brooklyn, New York City, a man was killed by a falling tree.Figure caption, BBC Weather presenter Helen Willetts look at the impacts of the powerful Nor'easterThe man has been identified as 56-year-old Leighton Brown, an employee of the New York City Housing Authority.According to local news, he was walking through east Brooklyn neighbourhood working an extra shift when the deadly incident occurred."We mourn deeply for the loss of Leighton Brown, a NYCHA employee who faithfully served Brooklyn residents and who was known for his warm personality," the Office of the NYC Public Advocate wrote on social media.The nor'easter has caused widespread power cuts. More than 160,000 households, nearly all in the north-eastern US, have lost electricity, according to tracker PowerOutage. More than 2,400 flights were delayed and another 1,199 grounded on Saturday, according to FlightAware.A full moon was projected to worsen coastal flooding.
articles.summary: 图注：观看：风暴席卷美国东北部，巨浪拍击海岸。作者：夸西·贾姆菲·阿谢杜（Kwasi Gyamfi Asiedu），51分钟前更新。美国东北部数以千万计的人置身于一场强劲的周末风暴路径之中，这场风暴带来了沿海洪水、停电、交通混乱以及体育场馆活动取消。美国国家气象局（NWS）表示，这场所谓的「东北风暴」（nor'easter）于周六给纽约市和波士顿等地区带来了「危险的沿海洪水和海滩状况、强风以及强降雨」。纽约州和新泽西州已宣布进入紧急状态，两地部分地区都遭遇了沿海洪水。从弗吉尼亚州到缅因州都预报有降雨和强风。在纽约市布鲁克林区，一名男子被倒下的树木砸中身亡。图注：BBC气象主持人海伦·威利茨（Helen Willetts）解析这场强劲东北风暴的影响。这名男子被确认为56岁的莱顿·布朗（Leighton Brown），是纽约市住房管理局（NYCHA）的员工。据当地新闻报道，事发时他正在东布鲁克林街区加班途中，不幸遭遇这起致命事件。纽约市公共倡导者办公室在社交媒体上写道：「我们深切哀悼莱顿·布朗的离世，他是一名NYCHA员工，忠实服务于布鲁克林居民，以热情的性格为人熟知。」这场东北风暴造成了大规模停电。据追踪机构PowerOutage统计，超过16万户家庭断电，几乎全部位于美国东北部。据FlightAware统计，周六有超过2400架次航班延误，另有1199架次航班停飞。预计满月将进一步加剧沿海洪水。

articles.title: Killer Christa Pike to be executed within days - but her defence say she's a victim too
articles.excerpt: Killer Christa Pike to be executed within days - but her defence say she's a victim tooImage source, Tennesse Department of CorrectionsImage caption, Christa Pike's lawyers have filed a clemency petition seeking to commute her sentence ahead of the 30 September execution date ByStephanie HegartyBBC World Service correspondentAshlee Sellars last heard from her friend Christa Pike earlier this week, when Pike texted her from her cell on death row as she prepares to be killed by lethal injection by the US state of Tennessee.Pike told Sellars she did not want any of her loved ones to be present on Wednesday when she is executed. "She doesn't want us to experience that," Sellars says.Sellars finds it hard to reconcile this woman, whom she has only known to be kind and protective, with the person who committed a heinous crime 31 years ago.Pike, now 50, was 18 when she and her boyfriend at the time, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and murdered Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old they met at a job training camp for troubled teens.The murder created a media frenzy in Knoxville, Tennessee in 1995, when Colleen was found with a pentagram - a symbol of Satanic ritual - carved into her chest.Pike had accused Colleen of insulting her and trying to steal her boyfriend. Two other residents at the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the murder before and after, and showed them a piece of Colleen's skull.A year later she was sentenced to death, while Shipp - who was 17 at the time - was given a life sentence with the possibility of parole. Now, after years of failed appeals, Pike's execution has been set. If it goes ahead, she will be the first woman put to death in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

articles.title: Woman charged with stealing from patients and staff at hospitals across Ontario
articles.excerpt: Police in Ontario, Canada, have charged a woman with 65 offences including fraud and theft for allegedly stealing from patients and staff at several healthcare centres in the province.Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) identified the suspect as Nassim Eronn, 34, from Burlington, a city 56km (34 miles) south of Toronto."The investigation was initiated following multiple reports of theft and fraud involving patients and staff members within healthcare facilities," police said in a statement to BBC News.They say the incidents under investigation began in February 2024 and continued until as recently as last month. The suspect worked at health centres across the province.The suspect faces charges including 34 counts of fraud under $5,000 (£3,800), 13 counts of theft under $5,000 and seven counts of disobeying a court order, according to police. Other charges include breach of trust and impersonation.OPP began investigating the woman in May after a report of theft when she worked at Orillia Soldiers' Memorial Hospital, about 130km north of Toronto."This investigation was prompted by several complaints of theft and fraud from patients and staff within the hospital," police said at the time.The investigation was expanded to cover more hospitals where further incidents were uncovered."Multiple search warrants were executed where significant amounts of property were seized," police said.

articles.title: German town bans 'stumbling stone' memorials to Nazi victims
articles.excerpt: There has been a wave of criticism in Germany after the town of Heidenau, near Dresden in Saxony, decided to ban "stumbling stone" memorials to victims of the Nazis.Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien told newspaper Bild that the ban was a "scandal".Since the 1990s, many towns in countries across Europe, including in Germany and Austria, have embedded small brass plaques in the streets in memory of Jews and other victims of Nazi atrocities.The plaques, called Stolpersteine in German, are often placed outside the houses where the victims used to live or work. They are frequently funded by donations.But now councillors from the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party and the conservative CDU in Heidenau have voted to ban stumbling stones in their town.The AfD in Saxony has been classified as extreme-right by German intelligence, a designation the party rejects.The motion in the town council said that many citizens felt that this form of commemoration of Nazi victims was inappropriate.

articles.title: Mother of woman found hanging in tree shocked as police say body was staged
articles.excerpt: Warning: This story contains distressing detailsThe mother of a woman found hanging in a tree in Mississippi has spoken of her shock after authorities said they believed her daughter was dead before her body was placed at the allegedly "staged" crime scene. Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old mother of four, was found hanging from a tree at an abandoned home in Jackson in August.The discovery sparked widespread fears in the majority-black city because of the state's deep history of racial violence and lynchings. But on Friday, police said that Fortune had been dead before her body was hanged from the tree."I have more questions now than what I did before," her mother Christy Spivey told the BBC.The Jackson Police Department said that the medical examiner who conducted Fortune's post-mortem examination had determined that her death was a homicide and that "the scene and the hanging were staged".Officials have not disclosed the exact cause of death or shared any potential motive behind the allegedly staged hanging.Three people have been arrested in the case, all of whom are black. "I was hoping to be more relieved," Spivey said, adding that the police had not specified how the three suspects were connected to her daughter - or why her death was allegedly staged in this way. "Still no cause of death, no date of death - nothing," she said. "What actually killed her?" Fortune's death left the local community on edge and lawmakers demanding federal probes. But the latest developments have created more confusion.Spivey told the BBC that getting the update from the coroner that her daughter did not die by hanging initially gave her peace - at least her daughter did not die in such a gruesome manner, she thought. "When the police called me, I started crying and thanked them and felt a little more at peace than I had before," she said.

articles.title: Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared
articles.excerpt: Figure caption, Disaster declared as heavy rain sparks Bangkok floodingBySean SeddonUpdated 27 September 2026A flood emergency disaster has been declared across Bangkok after more than 300mm (12in) of rain fell since Thursday, leaving roads in the Thai capital submerged. On Sunday, Bangkok's Metropolitan Authority said the rains have subsided, but canal water levels remain high. The city's governor has warned that the flooding is not yet over.People have been urged to stay at home and those living close to the city's network of canals have been advised to move their belongings to upper floors.Thunderstorms are common in Thailand at this time of year but extreme weather in recent days has inundated Bangkok's drainage system, causing traffic chaos on roads that are already famously congested. Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Canals across the Thai capital have burst their banks, leaving roads under waterSomkid Pheuk-ngam, a 67-year-old who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok, told the AFP news agency: "The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now."I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now."She said water levels in the city appeared to be worse than in 2011, when Bangkok was impacted by nationwide flooding.Hundreds were killed across Thailand then in an extreme weather event that lasted for three months. So far, no casualties have been reported in Bangkok from this latest flooding.The Thai Meteorological Service has forecast more heavy rain through the week, though the area of low pressure causing the downpours of recent days is expected to move towards central Thailand.Image source, Getty ImagesAll 50 of Bangkok's districts were declared emergency zones.On Saturday, Chadchart Sittipunt, the city's governor, said the east of the city had been hardest hit, AFP reported.He continued: "The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best.

articles.title: British national among six dead in building explosion close to Acropolis in Athens
articles.excerpt: Six people have died, including a British national, in an explosion that destroyed a building containing a holiday rental property in the historic centre of Athens.The blast on Friday happened in the Plaka area of the Greek capital, a neighbourhood close to tourist sites such as the Acropolis.Four American holidaymakers were among the dead, along with a UK national and Greek national - reportedly an elderly couple who lived in the same building. Pictures from the scene on Saturday showed emergency service workers searching through rubble, with a gas leak the suspected cause of the blast.All six bodies had been recovered by Saturday afternoon. Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said: "We are talking about an incredible disaster."The tourists were confirmed to be missing when they did not arrive for their flight at Athens airport later on Friday, news agency Reuters reported citing local police.The three-storey building completely collapsed due to the force of the blast, with neighbouring buildings damaged and debris scattered across the road.

articles.title: Why some Indian civil servants become heroes for doing their jobs
articles.excerpt: Among the thousands of civil servants who keep India's vast government machinery running, a small number become unlikely public figures every few years.Tukaram Mundhe, 51, is one of them.The commissioner of Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, he has led a series of enforcement drives since taking charge in May. His teams have inspected restaurants and other food businesses, uncovering pest infestations, poor hygiene and expired food.He has also highlighted large gaps between what hospitals pay for common medical supplies and what patients are charged.These actions have made Mundhe a social-media celebrity, with videos and images from inspections widely shared online. Hundreds of people have commented that they wished officers like him could be sent to fix food safety concerns in their state. Mundhe is not alone. In Gurugram, a suburb of Delhi, district town planner RS Batth has won praise for acting against illegal construction and encroachments.But why are these officials treated like heroes for doing their jobs?In India, civil servants are responsible for many services people rely on every day, from issuing documents to policing, food safety and healthcare. But many are also accused of delays, bribes and making people run from pillar to post.So when an official appears to cut through the red tape, the response can be surprisingly enthusiastic."What should have been normal has become exceptional," says retired civil servant Kamal Kant Jaswal.For many citizens, delays, bureaucratic hurdles and indifferent treatment have become so familiar that efficient governance now stands out as an exception, he adds. Mundhe is not the first official to gain recognition for doing exactly that.
articles.summary: 在维持印度庞大政府机器运转的数千名公务员中，每隔几年就会有一小部分人成为出人意料的公众人物。51岁的图卡拉姆·蒙德就是其中之一。作为马哈拉施特拉邦食品药品管理局的专员，他自5月上任以来领导了一系列执法行动。他的团队检查了餐馆和其他食品企业，发现了虫害滋生、卫生条件差和食品过期等问题。他还指出了医院为常见医疗用品支付的价格与向患者收取的费用之间的巨大差距。这些行动使蒙德成为社交媒体名人，检查过程中的视频和图片在网上广泛传播。数百人评论说，他们希望像他这样的官员能被派去解决他们所在邦的食品安全问题。蒙德并非个例。在德里郊区的古尔冈，地区城镇规划师RS·巴特因对非法建筑和侵占行为采取行动而赢得赞誉。但为什么这些官员仅仅因为履行职责就被当作英雄？在印度，公务员负责人们日常依赖的许多服务，从发放证件到治安、食品安全和医疗保健。但许多人也因拖延、贿赂和让人来回奔波而受到指责。因此，当一名官员似乎能打破繁文缛节时，公众的反应可能会异常热烈。退休公务员卡马尔·坎特·贾斯瓦尔说：「本应正常的事情却变成了例外。」他补充说，对许多公民来说，拖延、官僚障碍和冷漠对待已变得如此熟悉，以至于高效治理现在反而显得是一种例外。蒙德并不是第一个因为做到这一点而获得认可的官员。

articles.title: News media must stay relevant or 'society will struggle', says World News Day boss
articles.excerpt: World News Day has grown since it began in 2018, and its message that "trusted journalism matters" aims to highlight the role of news providers in investigating and explaining important events.It comes against a backdrop of what the recent Reuters Institute report described as "anxiety, disengagement, and cynicism" towards news among the public, "but also openness to new sources and formats, and continued belief in what news at its best can offer".Social media and video networks overtook news organisations' own websites and apps as the main source of online news last year, but are trusted less, the report said.In another report, published earlier this month, UK media regulator Ofcom, external also said people now get news from a wider variety of sources, with YouTube "growing rapidly" and 20% of people using AI tools to access news.But growing choice has gone hand-in-hand with greater uncertainty about who and what to believe, and traditional providers are still seen as more trustworthy, accurate and impartial than online platforms, Ofcom said.Brkic, who founded South Africa's Daily Maverick, accepts that the media landscape has changed, and said established news organisations must respond."The old days are not coming back. We need to form a new equilibrium, and the only way we can do it is that if we actually join forces," he said."If we continue like this, we're just going to be weak individual players waiting to be taken out.
articles.summary: 世界新闻日（World News Day）自2018年创办以来不断发展壮大，其「可信新闻至关重要」的理念旨在凸显新闻机构在调查和解释重要事件方面的作用。这一理念出台的背景是，路透社研究所最近的报告将公众对新闻的态度描述为「焦虑、疏离和怀疑」，「但同时也对新来源和新形式持开放态度，并继续相信新闻在最佳状态下所能提供的东西」。报告称，去年社交媒体和视频网络超越新闻机构自有的网站和应用，成为在线新闻的主要来源，但它们的可信度更低。在本月早些时候发布的另一份报告中，英国媒体监管机构Ofcom也表示，人们如今从更多样化的来源获取新闻，其中YouTube「增长迅速」，20%的人使用AI工具获取新闻。但Ofcom表示，选择的增多伴随着对谁和什么可信的更大不确定性，传统新闻提供者仍被认为比在线平台更可信、更准确、更公正。布爾基奇（Brkic）是南非《Daily Maverick》的创始人，他承认媒体格局已经改变，并表示老牌新闻机构必须做出回应。他说：「过去的日子不会回来了。我们需要形成一种新的平衡，而唯一的办法就是我们真正联合起来。」「如果我们继续这样下去，我们只会成为一个个弱小的个体玩家，等着被淘汰。」

articles.title: Before BTS and Blackpink, there was Big Bang: Now the Kings of K-pop are back
articles.excerpt: Image source, Timothy Norris/Getty ImagesImage caption, Taeyang, G-Dragon and Daesung of BigBang perform during the 2026 Coachella Valley Music and Arts FestivalByJiji Ahn A sea of glowing yellow crowns. Thousands of voices chanting in Korean.An explosive surge of energy as the opening synth riffs of Fantastic Baby shatter the stadium air. Big Bang is back.Fourteen years after their first major European shows, and after a decade marked by military service, member departures and legal scandals, the South Korean group played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Saturday as part of their 20th anniversary world tour.Inside the near-capacity venue, the crowd did not just watch a concert - they stepped into a significant moment in K-pop history.As the band emerged in their trademark high-fashion, glittering outfits, the crowd danced freely, setting the tone for an evening that felt less like a routine tour stop and more like a homecoming.Image caption, Inside Tottenham Hotspur StadiumFor fans, it is a long-awaited reunion. But the significance of Big Bang's return extends beyond nostalgia.Years before BTS were selling out Wembley Stadium and Blackpink were headlining Hyde Park, Big Bang were already proving Korean pop could succeed far beyond Asia.The group filled arenas across the West, collaborated with major American artists, experimented with hip-hop and electronic music, and turned their own fashion and creative identities into part of their appeal.Having attended their European debut at Wembley Arena in 2012, the shift in atmosphere on Saturday was striking.Where their original UK shows were driven by a hunger to prove themselves and promote a new album, this return as a trio, comprising G-Dragon, Taeyang and Daesung, felt entirely crafted for their dedicated community.

articles.title: Young people in China are fangirling over a professor who gets their anxiety
articles.excerpt: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Young Chinese people are anxious about their future in a rapdily changing countryByFan Wang"A star sent from the heavens," is how Zihan Han describes the man she's become a huge fan of recently, a man who young Chinese people call an "idol".Except this is no pop singer or movie star, but a 54-year old anthropologist. Professor Biao Xiang has become an unlikely guide for an increasingly disillusioned generation.And it's because of what he talks about: anxiety and how to navigate it.China's economy and tech have grown at breakneck speed, but there is plenty worrying its Gen Z, from jobs to romantic prospects to the sheer pressure of keeping up."The transition from school to the real world brings a lot of uncertainty now, and people often feel anxious because they don't know how to face it," says a 23-year-old Chinese graduate who didn't want to reveal her name because she was worried speaking to foreign media might affect her chances of finding a job back home."People need an anchor in their life. And his words make us feel there is someone that gets me."She and Zihan were among some 500 people - mostly Chinese diaspora - who piled into an auditorium recently in Singapore. Xiang spoke for more than an hour in Mandarin before he took questions. When it ended, dozens queued to meet and take photos with him. The Chinese grad called it "an academic fan meeting".Xiang has been interviewed by major Chinese outlets and has travelled to top Chinese campuses to talk, including at his alma mater, the prestigious Peking University – one talk earlier this year was live-streamed because the auditorium was full.

articles.title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever
articles.excerpt: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear foreverImage source, Project Pressure/Klaus ThymannImage caption, Only small patches of snow remain on Papua's Sudirman RangeByAbraham UtamaBBC IndonesiaThe mountains of Papua are not far from the equator, but they've been topped with "eternal snow" for centuries.The peaks in this Indonesian region on the world's second-largest island, just north of Australia, have offered scientists countless insights into the Earth's climate history.They're also the epicentre of the spiritual universe for many Papuans - a Mecca or a Vatican, as one activist puts it.But now, nearly all the snow is gone.A century ago, the 300km (190-mile) stretch of the Sudirman Range had snow and permanent ice on all four of its major peaks.But now there are only small areas around Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, with any snow at all. These are expected to entirely disappear in a year or two.Glacier cover around the peak has shrunk from nearly 1,900 hectares (4,700 acres) in the 19th Century to about 16 hectares (40 acres) today. Almost entire glaciers have vanished within a human lifetime."There is a profound unfairness in this," says Marie Šabacká, a Czech glacier ecologist who travelled to Puncak Jaya last March in a bid to be among the last scientists to study Papua's "eternal snow".She says the tropical glaciers in Papua are unique because they are separated from other glacier systems by thousands of kilometres. Papua is home to the "last remaining tropical ice" between the Andes and Himalayas.Ice cores taken from the slopes of Puncak Jaya preserve a record of climate history.

articles.title: Watch: BBC reports from the front-line of an escalating war in Yemen
articles.excerpt: In rare access to Yemen's conflict zone, the BBC has travelled with government forces from Taiz through checkpoints to the line where the Houthi control ends and no man's land begins. Saudi-backed pro-government forces are battling to push back Houthi fighters, who swept down the coast of the Red Sea earlier this month, taking control of a key shipping chokepoint and escalating Yemen's civil war.From the front-line a drone is heard above, which a soldier accompanying the crew in south-western Yemen said is usually followed by an attack. Within about 10 minutes, after the crew had driven away, the loud thuds of strikes followed, senior international investigations correspondent Nawal Al-Maghafi reports.

articles.title: Watch: The ups and downs of SpaceX's 13 Starship test flights
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is planning to carry out its 14th Starship rocket test flight on Monday.If successful, it will be the first Starship to go in orbit around the Earth and the furthest one has ever flown.The mission is set to complete approximately six orbits around the planet over a 10-hour flight.But as the BBC's Ricky Boleto reports, there have been many ups and downs along the way.

articles.title: Are claims of a white genocide in South Africa real?
articles.excerpt: An Afrikaner lobby group has displayed thousands of white crosses on the National Mall in Washington DC, saying they represent the victims of a genocide of white people in South Africa.But South Africa's new ambassador to the US, Roelf Meyer, says that the notion of a mass attack on the white Afrikaner minority in South Africa does not exist.Meanwhile, the Trump administration is planning to admit up to 17,500 additional white Afrikaners as refugees over the next 12 months, according to a notice sent to Congress on Tuesday.The BBC's North America correspondent Ione Wells explains what role the US has played in the claim of a genocide.

articles.title: Watch: Bangkok declared flood disaster zone
articles.excerpt: The whole of Bangkok has been declared a flood disaster zone as authorities try to pump days of floodwater into the sea. Heavy rain over the last two days has overwhelmed Bangkok's water systems, with more rain forecast on Sunday. People have been urged to stay at home and those living close to the city's network of canals have been advised to move their belongings to upper floors. BBC South East Asia Correspondent Jonathan Head reports from Bangkok

articles.title: Why an international arrest warrant didn't stop Netanyahu's US trip
articles.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended his country's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly on 24 September. His speech occurred while an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court for alleged war crimes is in effect. The BBC's Nada Tawfik explains why Netanyahu was not arrested after speaking at the UN General Assembly.SubsectionUS & CanadaPublished2 days agoRelated topicsUN General AssemblyIsrael-Gaza warIsraelUnited NationsBenjamin Netanyahu

articles.title: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say
articles.excerpt: Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police.The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.In a separate statement, police said 10 people had been killed in a mass shooting at an entertainment venue selling grilled meat, known as shisanyama, in Lwandle, near Cape Town. Another 11 people were wounded in that shooting. Police said they were searching for multiple suspects, without giving an exact number.The two attacks happened days after a mass shooting by three gunmen at a house party near the east-coast city of Durban killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.No arrests had been made in the two latest mass shootings, police said.South Africa has struggled with high rates of violent crime for years, but the series of mass shootings this week were shocking even to a country used to some of the highest violent crime rates in the world.“This ​cannot go on like this,” South Africa’s president, Cyril Ramaphosa, told local TV news channels. “This is the level of criminality that we must bring down, and our security forces are now going ⁠to continue pulling out all stops.”A man clears the debris in a shisanyama in Lwandle after gunmen stormed the premises.

articles.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys
articles.excerpt: Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops.As a result of the population boom, troops of chacma baboons on the city’s peninsula regularly rip off roof sheeting, sneak into unlocked cars and raid food pantries. Some monkeys are now staying up late into the night to break into homes in Simon’s Town and nab snacks from convenience stores. Residents can no longer barbecue or host garden parties for fear of the marauding baboons.A community volunteer reminds drivers to slow down to protect baboons in Cape Town, May 2022. Photograph: Xinhua/Shutterstock“It’s depreciated property values because it’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces and paw prints, and you know they’re coming every day,” said Justin O’Riain, a behavioural ecologist at the University of Cape Town who has long studied the local baboons.Cape Town’s geography is partially to blame. Much of the problem is confined to the Cape Peninsula, a narrow sliver of land stretching from the city centre to Cape Point. Here, baboons are boxed in between the steep, protected area of Table Mountain national park and the sprawling urban development that stretches to the Atlantic Ocean.“The underlying issue is that baboons will seek low-lying land.

articles.title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war
articles.excerpt: There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.On Sunday, seven armed groups from around the country, including the TPLF, announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, aimed at deposing the government in Addis Ababa. Then, on Wednesday, the TPLF seized control of three airports from federal police. The state-owned carrier, Ethiopian Airlines, said it had suspended flights to the region “due to the current situation”.The TPLF also launched attacks into Afar and Amhara. A humanitarian source in Afar told Agence France-Presse there were heavy artillery attacks by the group on Thursday as they attempted to take control of the town of Yallo, near the Tigrayan border.Flights to the historic Ethiopian town of Lalibela were also suspended on Thursday because of nearby fighting, while people in Tigray stocked up ⁠on food and cash, with one resident telling Reuters that people there feared they could face siege conditions similar to those during the previous war.A resident of Adigrat, a city close to the Eritrean border, ‌described panic-buying and shops emptying. “Food shortages are worsening as market shelves sit empty … Essential medicines remain scarce and astronomically expensive,” he told Reuters.

articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years
articles.excerpt: A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange.Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures.The company is understood to be hoping to raise about $800m (£601m) from the initial public offering (IPO) and is targeting a valuation of $8bn to $9bn, which would make it one of London’s largest listings in recent years.Airtel Money has 53 million monthly active users across 13 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, including Uganda, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.Sunil Bharti Mittal controls Bharti Enterprises. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty ImagesIt operates through a network of branches and kiosks, which enable customers to load money on to their phones, withdraw cash and access other money services, and the company generated revenues of just under $1.4bn in the last financial year.Airtel Money’s parent company is Airtel Africa, a telecoms provider that is part of the Indian conglomerate Bharti Enterprises, which is ultimately controlled by the billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal. Airtel Africa is already listed on the FTSE 100 but said it wanted Airtel Money to be listed separately.“From a company perspective, [the listing] gives us flexibility for the future,” said Airtel Money’s chief executive, Ian Ferrao.“We evaluated multiple [stock] exchanges, including the Middle East because we’ve got a headquarters in Dubai, along with European and North American exchanges. Ultimately, shareholders felt that London was the right choice.

articles.title: Top South African police officer charged with raping woman, 18, and grooming 16-year-old girl
articles.excerpt: One of South Africa’s most senior police officers has been charged with raping an 18-year-old woman and grooming a 16-year-old girl, as the country’s police face allegations of corruption and failing to tackle violence against women and girls.Shadrack Sibiya, who was already suspended from his role as deputy national police commissioner over allegations he interfered with political killings investigations, was arrested on Monday. He is facing charges of rape, people trafficking, promoting the sexual grooming of a child and two counts of grooming a child.Sibiya appeared briefly in a Johannesburg court on Tuesday. He was then taken to prison in the capital, Pretoria, before a bail hearing on 29 September, as prosecutors had argued he was an escape risk.South Africa is reeling after the discovery of nine women’s bodies across Ekurhuleni, the municipality east of Johannesburg, in September. Meanwhile, the Madlanga Commission judicial inquiry has been examining allegations of corruption and criminality within the police for the last year.Puleng Dimpane, the acting national police commissioner, said: “Police officers are entrusted with protecting women and children. They cannot themselves be implicated in conduct that undermines this responsibility. As the country continues to confront the scourge of gender-based violence and femicide, there can be no room for anyone within the police service who is alleged to abuse their position or violate the rights of women and children.”Sibiya is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman at a hotel in May in the Sandton business district of Johannesburg. The alleged rape took place “whilst she was passed out due to intoxication administered by the accused”, according to a copy of the charge sheet.The alleged grooming of the 16-year-old girl took place over WhatsApp between 20 July and 3 August, according to the charge sheet.

articles.title: Mighty Sparrow, the Trinidad and Tobago singer known as the ‘calypso king of the world’, dies aged 91
articles.excerpt: Slinger Francisco, known on stage as the Mighty Sparrow and dubbed the “calypso king of the world”, has died aged 91.Francisco, who got his breakthrough in calypso music with his 1956 hit song Jean and Dinah, died peacefully surrounded by his family in New York on Sunday, his family said in a statement.His death came after a “brief illness,” the statement said without disclosing any other details.“He was an institution in the entertainment industry, well admired for his skill and finesse as a singer, songwriter and mentor; beloved by many,” Francisco’s family said.Mighty Sparrow performs at the Melkweg in 1989 in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. Photograph: Frans Schellekens/RedfernsThe Mighty Sparrow will be remembered as “a defining voice of our culture, a master storyteller and a towering figure whose music helped carry calypso from Trinidad and Tobago to the world,” the Trinbago Unified Calypsonians’ Organisation said in a statement.Born in the coastal town of Grand Roy, Grenada, in July 1935, Francisco was just a toddler when he migrated with his parents to Trinidad and Tobago in 1937.Trinidad and Tobago is the birthplace of calypso music, and was where the name and persona of the Mighty Sparrow emerged to produce a list of hit songs in the genre: Both of Them, Congo Man, Mr. Walker, The Lizard and many more.Birdie, as Francisco was also affectionately known, recorded hundreds of songs in a career that spanned six decades.
articles.summary: 斯林格·弗朗西斯科，艺名「 mighty Sparrow 」（强大的麻雀），被誉为「世界卡利普索之王」，于91岁高龄去世。弗朗西斯科1956年凭借热门歌曲《Jean and Dinah》在卡利普索音乐界取得突破。其家人发表声明称，他于周日（9月28日）在纽约在家人的陪伴下安详离世。声明称，他的去世发生在一场「短暂的疾病」之后，但未透露其他细节。弗朗西斯科的家人表示：「他是娱乐界的一座丰碑，作为歌手、词曲作者和导师，他的技艺和精湛表现广受赞誉；深受许多人爱戴。」（配图说明：1989年，Mighty Sparrow 在荷兰阿姆斯特丹的 Melkweg 演出。摄影：Frans Schellekens/Redferns。）特立尼达和多巴哥统一卡利普索歌手组织在一份声明中表示，Mighty Sparrow 将被铭记为「我们文化的一个决定性声音、一位讲故事的大师，以及一位巨人，他的音乐帮助将卡利普索从特立尼达和多巴哥带到了全世界」。弗朗西斯科1935年7月出生于格林纳达的沿海小镇格兰德罗伊，1937年随父母移居特立尼达和多巴哥时还是个蹒跚学步的孩子。特立尼达和多巴哥是卡利普索音乐的诞生地，也是 Mighty Sparrow 这个名字和形象崭露头角的地方，他创作了一系列该流派的热门歌曲：《Both of Them》《Congo Man》《Mr. Walker》《The Lizard》等等。弗朗西斯科还被人们亲切地称为「小鸟」，在长达60年的职业生涯中录制了数百首歌曲。

articles.title: Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico's Baja braces for major Hurricane Polo
articles.excerpt: Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms.Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19kph). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph (165kph).Nolo was expected to strengthen further and turn toward the north-west by Sunday night, though the US National Hurricane Center said the storm’s center would remain well south and south-west of the Hawaiian Islands. The storm was expected to approach the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, a national conservation area, early this week.Forecasters said Nolo’s outer bands could cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides, with parts of the Big Island possibly getting up to 20in (50cm ) of rain. Heavy rain also was expected on the other islands.“Don’t venture out if you don’t have to into the dangerous flooding environment, but also high winds. We can have trees and power lines down,” said Michael Brennan, director of the National Hurricane Center.Heavy rain fell across the southern part of the Big Island on Saturday afternoon, prompting partial closures of one of the main highways linking Kailua-Kona in the west to Hilo in the east.Members of the Hawaii army national guard help a resident leave his home as rainwater from nearby Hurricane Nolo floods a section of Mamalahoa highway on Saturday. Photograph: Gregory Bull/APNear Naalehu, at the island’s southern point, National Guard members were seen guiding a man driving through flooded streets as he tried to leave his home during a downpour.
articles.summary: 「诺洛」飓风周日正逐渐远离夏威夷群岛，但这条仍在从先前风暴中恢复的岛链部分地区，强降雨、山洪暴发和强风的威胁仍持续存在。「诺洛」位于火奴鲁鲁西南偏南约365英里（585公里）处，正以约12英里/小时（19公里/小时）的速度远离大岛。但夏威夷县民防局表示，由于「诺洛」最大持续风速已升至115英里/小时（165公里/小时），高风警告、大风提示和高浪提示在周日晚间之前仍对该岛部分地区有效。预计「诺洛」还会进一步增强，并在周日晚间转向西北方向，不过美国国家飓风中心表示，风暴中心将始终位于夏威夷群岛以南和西南方向较远处。预计这场风暴将于本周初接近帕帕哈瑙莫夸基亚国家海洋保护区这一国家保育区。预报员称，「诺洛」的外围雨带可能引发危及生命的洪水和泥石流，大岛部分地区降雨量可能高达20英寸（50厘米）。其他岛屿也预计将出现强降雨。国家飓风中心主任迈克尔·布伦南表示：「如果不是非出去不可，就不要进入危险的洪水环境，同时还要注意强风。树木和电线可能被吹倒。」周六下午，大岛南部普降大雨，导致连接西部凯鲁瓦-科纳和东部希洛的一条主要公路部分关闭。在夏威夷军队国民警卫队成员帮助一名居民离开家园时，附近「诺洛」飓风的雨水淹没了马马拉霍亚公路的一段。照片：格雷戈里·布尔/美联社。在岛屿最南端的纳阿莱胡附近，有人看到国民警卫队成员在倾盆大雨中引导一名男子驾车穿过被洪水淹没的街道，试图离开他的家。

articles.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering
articles.excerpt: While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific.Ecuador’s president, Daniel Noboa, right, presents the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, with Ecuador’s highest ranking National Order of Merit, the Grand Cross, at Carondelet palace in Quito, on 9 September. Photograph: Dolores Ochoa/APOn 8 September, a day before Rubio arrived, a US patrol vessel intercepted the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador.“The gringos were all armed as if they were going to war,” said the boat’s captain, Mero Calderón, 50. “I tried to show them our catch to prove that we were there working, but they wouldn’t listen,” he added.A US patrol vessel intercepting the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador. Photograph: US Southern Command/X“They brought two huge bombs aboard, took us to their ship, handcuffed and blindfolded us, and blew our boat to pieces,” said Calderón, who along with five other fishers, was handed over to local authorities.But another 10 crew members were fishing farther out to sea in a smaller boat that was not equipped to make it back to shore. The Ecuadorian navy only rescued them on 10 September, when Rubio was already in Peru preparing to return to the US.Ten crew members from the five skiffs belonging to the vessel Don Rufo, after they were located and taken aboard the BAE Atahualpa, following air-maritime search and reconnaissance operations conducted by the Ecuadorian navy.

articles.title: Lula bans fixed-odds sports betting a week before Brazilian elections
articles.excerpt: The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt.The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.The provisional executive order comes into force immediately but will need congressional approval within 120 days to remain in effect. It prohibits new deposits into accounts and gives users of betting platforms until 5 October to withdraw their funds.Lula’s government has also drafted a bill to establish criminal offences related to fixed-odds betting – the most common and dominant type of online sports betting – such as promoting them and using personal data to solicit punters.“I made the decision to take a hard, drastic and necessary measure,” he told journalists in São Paulo. “It’s like cancer, you take out the tumour, or the tumour will kill us.”Lula had also criticised the betting industry earlier this week at the UN general assembly, accusing it of “transforming addiction into profit” and of “destroying homes”.Polls suggest a ban enjoys widespread support among Brazilians. Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula’s main rival in the coming election, accused the current leader of an “electoral measure”.Brazil’s president has sharply criticised online betting at least since April, when he called for a ban. The public backlash against it grew during the Fifa World Cup when advertisements were ubiquitous and the number of people betting surged.Betting and gambling are estimated to cost Brazilian society 38.8bn reais (£5.6bn) annually and increases suicide and depression, according to a 2025 study by the nonprofit Institute of Studies for Health Policies.The country’s central bank estimated last year that Brazilians spend about 30bn reais on bets each month.

articles.title: Michigan CEO loses job after posting AI-made image of her family in ‘Lake America’ sweaters
articles.excerpt: The CEO of a Michigan credit union is no longer employed there, according to the organization, after she posted on social media what appeared to be an AI-generated image of her and her family wearing sweaters emblazoned with the Donald Trump-associated words “Lake America”.In the statement recently announcing that Jane Smith would no longer be its CEO, Family First Credit Union also apologized “for the concern, disappointment and pain this situation has caused”.Smith had been the chief executive officer of the Family First Credit Union when she posed for a family photo at the Detroit airport en route to Halifax, Canada. She reportedly used ChatGPT to edit the family’s sweaters to say Lake America, which since late August has been the name that Trump ordered the US’s federal government agencies to use for Lake Ontario amid the president’s trade war with Canada.Smith then shared the image on Facebook on 11 September – the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks in the US – along with the caption: “Like our sweatshirts? Not sure Canada will.”The post ended with “Lol lol”. It went viral and then provoked backlash from people in Canada – where a portion of the lake is.Those online users found it disrespectful, and the post has since been deleted according to Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) News.Many in the comments highlighted that the post was particularly insensitive, given Halifax’s role in hosting thousands of stranded airplane passengers who were diverted there when US airspace closed on the day of the 9/11 attacks.As the controversy intensified, Family First Credit Union – based in Saginaw, Michigan – said it was reviewing the situation. Smith, meanwhile, apologized, expressing regret, maintaining that the post was the result of poor judgment and saying that she understood why it would be offensive.“We weren’t trying to make a political statement,” Smith told the Detroit television news station WJRT.

articles.title: Two giant pandas arrive in Atlanta from China after Xi-Trump summit
articles.excerpt: Two giant pandas from China arrived in Atlanta, Georgia, on Sunday morning as part of an agreement between the Chinese and American governments.While in Washington DC for a three-day summit with Donald Trump, Chinese president Xi Jinping announced that the pandas would arrive in Atlanta in the coming days. The loan of the pandas to the Atlanta zoo was one of the few concrete outcomes to come out of Xi’s state visit with the US president, which saw expressions of goodwill between the leaders, but no fixes to any of the longstanding differences between the two countries.Atlanta said farewell to its last pandas in 2024, leaving the zoo without the bears. The new agreement was announced back in April, but without any dates.A farewell ceremony is held on Saturday for giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang at Chengdu research base of giant panda breeding. Photograph: Xu Bingjie/Xinhua/APPing Ping and Fu Shuang are the two adult pandas that will be on loan to Zoo Atlanta for 10 years as part of the agreement. They departed Chengdu in south-western China early on Sunday aboard a dedicated “FedEx Panda Express” Boeing 777 aircraft, officials said. A new agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association makes Atlanta one of three zoos in the US to house giant pandas.Ping Ping and Fu Shuang were born in 2020 and were kept at the Chengdu research base of giant panda breeding. The male Ping Ping has dark black circles around his eyes, while Fu Shuang, a female, has a forehead that protrudes a bit, according to the Xinhua News Agency.China has long used the pandas as part of its diplomacy globally, deploying the bears in loan programs as expressions of goodwill and letting loan agreements lapse when tensions arise.Xi had said the loan program was an example of “friendship between the Chinese and Americans”.

articles.title: Pomp over progress in Xi’s US summit with Trump is a win for China
articles.excerpt: If the Beijing meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in May was the “stalemate summit”, the second round of talks between the presidents of the US and China this week seemed to give up entirely on the idea of breakthroughs.Instead, it was described as a celebration of “diplotainment” rather than diplomacy, where pomp prevailed over progress and where one of the main outcomes was the news that two giant pandas would soon be sent from China to Atlanta zoo.Trump rolled out the red carpet for Xi’s arrival on Wednesday and broke with decades of precedent to meet the Chinese leader at Joint Base Andrews. Thus began a three-day state visit that involved a tour of Trump’s new helipad and the Marine One helicopter, and a 90-minute meeting that Trump described as “great” and that revealed, according to Trump, that Xi “has great interest in granite”.“The biggest takeaway is that Trump has been displaying an extraordinary degree of deference to Xi Jinping,” said Julian Gewirtz, who served as a senior China official in the Biden administration.But what of actual substance? Expectations going into the summit were low. But the outcomes somehow still fell short.Expectations going into the summit were low. Photograph: Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty ImagesOne of the biggest issues in the US-China relationship is trade. Last year, as Trump unveiled successive rounds of tariffs on Chinese goods, the White House accused China of unfair practices that it said contributed to the loss of 3.7m US jobs and inflated the trade deficit. The tariffs were supposed to suppress the volume of Chinese imports to the US and put pressure on China.To some degree, they worked. The US trade deficit with China in 2025 fell to $200bn, down from nearly $300bn in 2024.

articles.title: At Trump meeting, Xi Jinping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict
articles.excerpt: Xi Jinping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put the US and China on a military collision course amid rising tensions over artificial intelligence, trade and Taiwan.At the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House, the Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could steer the two competing superpowers away from future military conflict and on to a road of mutual gain.Rather than confrontation, conditions for “achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again go hand in hand” and should be the goal, Xi said, citing Trump’s political catchphrase.“We should strengthen communication. China and the United States are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialogue, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust,” said Xi, with Trump looking on.“We should coexist in peace. China and the United States, as two major countries, stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation. Our two militaries should maintain regular dialog and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention.”With such conditions in place, Xi said, “the Thucydides trap can be overcome”, referring to the phenomenon, defined by the Greek historian, of tensions that arise when an emerging power challenges the dominance of an established power.Xi invoked the phrase in his meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, asking the US president how he planned to avoid it.His proposals for lessening tensions – which also included the invitation of 100,000 young Americans to visit China on student exchanges – come amid a period of intense competition between the two powers over artificial intelligence and trade, with each side imposing tariffs on the other.Trump and Xi speak next to Marine One at the White House.

articles.title: Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?
articles.excerpt: One is an authoritarian who represses the media and has a strong allergy to democratic elections. The other is head of the Chinese Communist party.Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, to the White House on Thursday, setting the stage for a scene quite unlike anything the august old building has seen over more than two centuries.“Remarkably,” observed the US president, “this is our first time meeting together here at the White House, and as President Xi has already seen, a lot has changed since he was last here.”While Xi remained poker-faced, only a brief look around a grand foyer bedecked with American and Chinese flags would have verified Trump’s statement. On one wall, where an official portrait of Barack Obama once hung, was the dramatic image of a bloodied Trump with fist raised urging his supporters to “fight!” after a failed assassination attempt.And while Chinese state media had been welcomed onto the White House grounds, many US journalists had not, thanks to Trump’s ban on CNN, MS Now and Politico. Michael McFaul, a former US diplomat, described the vivid contrast as “wrong and embarrassing”.That was hard to deny, given that China ranks 178th in Reporters Without Borders’ press freedom index, ahead of only North Korea and Eritrea (the US, for the record, is down to 64th). But it also made perfect sense because, whereas past presidents sought to make China more like the US, Trump evidently aspires to make the US more like China.Trump and Xi walk along the Colonnade at the White House. Photograph: Annabelle Gordon/Abaca/ShutterstockThe deference was deafening.

articles.title: Rick Wakeman performs piano concert to 150 rescued moon bears in Vietnam
articles.excerpt: Rick Wakeman has played to all kinds of people around the globe, but he has now performed to an audience he had never encountered before – an enclosure of 150 bears.The former Yes musician, who has gone on to have a prolific solo career, played the piano at a Vietnamese bear sanctuary.“Before you ask, I won’t be playing the teddy bear’s picnic,” he joked ahead of the performance. Wakeman, who is a supporter of animal welfare causes and has rescue dogs and cats of his own, is conducting the concert to raise awareness of moon bears kept in cruel conditions for the extraction of their bile.He said he was a bit worried about how hot it is going to be. “You know the heatwave we had in England? It’s double that,” he said. “They offered to rig up a fan for me, but I figured that will just blow more hot air around.”A moon bear at the bear sanctuary in Tam Dao national park, Vietnam. Photograph: Luong Thai Linh/EPAHis concert was performed live on a Yamaha grand piano positioned in Animals Asia’s bear sanctuary in the Tam Dao national park, and Wakeman had written some new compositions especially for rescued bears.Asked whether the bears would enjoy the music, he said: “They’ve not got much choice, really. It’s a well-known fact that all animals react to music, especially gentle melodic music. So what I am going to do is piano music that is melodic, and I can only hope that they will come up to the perimeter of the sanctuary and have a listen.”Rick Wakeman plays piano at bear sanctuaryWakeman has been sponsoring rescue bears since 2016 and recently adopted a new one: “He’s only 20 months old, a big fella, I went to see him today. He came out right to the edge and stood on his back legs and just stared at me, it was brilliant.”Bile is extracted from bears for traditional Chinese medicine by putting a needle into their gall bladder and drawing it out.

articles.title: Australia news live: Mike Baird resigns as Cricket Australia chair; RBA expected to hike cash rate to 4.6%
articles.excerpt: From 38m agoMike Baird to step down as chair of Cricket AustraliaFormer NSW premier Mike Baird will step down as the chair of Cricket Australia at the body’s next annual general meeting in October.Baird has been chair since early 2023 and led Cricket Australia’s push to privatize the Big Bash Leagues clubs. Both NSW and Queensland have opposed the plan.In a statement, Baird said: double quotation markI believe Australian cricket continues to be well led by the CA Board. Their mix of significant experience and passion for the game gives me great confidence for the future. … I have been incredibly proud to play a role in the oversight of cricket on the CNSW Board and, over the past six years, the CA Board, including almost four as chair. David Boon, a former Test batter, will take over as interim chair on 28 October as a process to find a new full-time chair begins.Key events2h agoBogong moths descend along NSW coast during annual migration3h agoGallagher says final budget outcome will show $6bn improvement3h agoInterest rate hike looms as inflation stubbornly high3h agoChalmers and Gallagher to present final budget outcomeBenita KolovosParamedics to take the lead in Victoria mental health call outsParamedics will take the lead in mental health emergency callouts – not police – under a new agreement announced by Victoria’s health minister, Ingrid Stitt, this morning.Under the new mental health crisis response protocols, signed by Ambulance Victoria, Victoria police and the health department, these callouts will be treated as a “health-led” response rather than a law-and-order matter.Victoria’s mental health royal commission recommended in 2021 that paramedics become first responders to Triple Zero calls for mental health crises.
articles.summary: 在新南威尔士州前州长迈克·贝尔德（Mike Baird）将辞去澳大利亚板球协会（Cricket Australia）主席一职，于10月举行的下一届年度股东大会上正式卸任。贝尔德自2023年初起担任该职务，任内力推将Big Bash联赛各俱乐部私有化的计划，但该计划遭到新南威尔士州和昆士兰州两地的反对。贝尔德在声明中表示：「我相信澳大利亚板球在CA董事会的领导下依然方向正确。他们兼具丰富经验和对这项运动的热忱，让我对未来充满信心……我非常自豪能在新州板球协会董事会以及过去六年中在CA董事会监督板球事务，其中包括近四年的主席任期。」前测试赛击球手大卫·布恩（David Boon）将于10月28日起担任临时主席，同时启动寻找新任全职主席的程序。其他要闻包括：博贡蛾（Bogong moths）在一年一度的迁徙中沿新州海岸南下；加拉格尔表示最终预算结果将显示60亿澳元的改善；通胀居高不下令加息迫在眉睫；查默斯和加拉格尔将公布最终预算结果。此外，维州卫生部长英格丽德·斯泰特（Ingrid Stitt）今晨宣布新协议，维州心理健康紧急呼叫将由急救人员而非警察主导响应。根据维州救护车机构、维州警方与卫生部门签署的新心理健康危机响应规程，这类呼叫将被视为「卫生主导」的响应，而非治安事务。维州心理健康皇家委员会曾在2021年建议由急救人员作为心理健康危机三零（Triple Zero）呼叫的第一响应者。

articles.title: Shannon felt a ‘sense of doom’ as she sought justice for sexual assault. A new NSW program hopes to alleviate that
articles.excerpt: It took Shannon Stokes two years and 11 days to successfully prosecute her former boyfriend for sexual assault and domestic violence offences. The lengthy trial left her feeling as though “there wasn’t going to be an end in sight”.Prosecutors secured convictions on nine of the 11 charges, and he was later sentenced to five years in prison.Stokes, 28, from New South Wales, said a “sense of doom” throughout the trial was compounded by a lack of appropriate legal assistance as she navigated the justice system, a world she said felt “so alien” to her.She recalled receiving pamphlets in the lead-up to the trial that she said were “more or less about how to look presentable” in court.“I also had a few pieces of paper handed to me on the day going into that courtroom, and that was what I had to kind of go off … it just makes you feel so isolated and like a number in the system rather than a person who has actually been victimised by violence.”Experts say Stokes’ experience is common among sexual assault victim-survivors pursuing justice. Sarah Rosenberg, the executive director of the victim-led network With You We Can and an advocate for justice reform, has long called for greater support for victim-survivors navigating the legal system.“They’re expected to navigate a very isolating, very complex system entirely alone,” she said.

articles.title: One Nation boss called David Farley an ‘asshole’ in lead-up to Farrer byelection, text messages reveal
articles.excerpt: One Nation’s general manager, Kelvin Morton – brought in by the party to improve its vetting processes – referred to David Farley as an “asshole” just days before Farley’s historic Farrer byelection win for the party in May.In a series of text messages seen by Guardian Australia, Morton responds to a news article published in the Sydney Morning Herald about infighting among senior party figures over Farley’s previously undeclared support for the Labor party.“Shit stirring,” he writes.“We need to do way better with our candidate selection – we need to stop finding these assholes … or letting them find us.“I guess this might nail David’s colours to us a little more. He’s sworn allegiance in the face of all the concerns being raised – he’d look like a completely untrustworthy snake if he jumped ship after the election – he’d be ruined forever.”A One Nation party spokesperson said that Farley was “a dedicated One Nation MP”.“The comments made do not reflect the view of the party.“The only untrustworthy snake is the person who leaked the text messages.”Tensions between Farley and other One Nation MPs and staff have reportedly been high since he was elected to parliament, with the party having to publicly criticise him after he claimed One Nation’s migration policy was not dissimilar to the Labor government’s. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here Morton, who claims on his LinkedIn to be a “strategic business transformation leader” with vast experience with some of the world’s biggest companies, was appointed as general manager in February.At the time, he said the party’s national executive had wanted him to build a “professional, scalable, and legally robust organisation capable of outright victory at the next general election”.

articles.title: RBA expected to hike cash rate to 4.6%, its highest level since 2011
articles.excerpt: Australia’s key interest rate is expected to hit its highest level since 2011, drag down house prices and add more than $100 to typical monthly mortgage repayments.The Reserve Bank board is poised to hike the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.6% on Tuesday, which would be the fourth increase in 2026 and push typical home loan interest rates to 6.5%.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailFor someone with an average-sized new mortgage of $731,000, now paying a rate of 6.2%, an increase would add about $119 to their $4,477 monthly repayments. That would take the total rise in repayments since January to nearly $480.The share of borrowers behind on their home loan repayments is small but rising, S&P data analysed by Westpac shows.Household budgets have also been strained by rising petrol prices amid the US war on Iran, now 80c higher since the start of the year, adding $44 to the cost of filling up a vehicle with a 55-litre tank.Consumer spending is already slowing, with Commonwealth Bank data showing households cut back on purchases of education, motor vehicles and household goods in August.House prices would fall further after a fourth rate rise. Comparison website Canstar estimated a hike would cut $11,200 from the borrowing capacity of someone earning an average annual full-time wage of $108,650, taking the total lost borrowing power to $47,400.Shrinking borrowing capacities have locked buyers out of markets.

articles.title: British celebrities beat AI companies lobbying to get free use of their work. They have a warning for Australia
articles.excerpt: If you want to state the case against copyright reform in Australia, get Kylie Minogue’s phone number.If there is one lesson to be learned from a similar battle in the UK, high-profile members of the creative industries make a difference. They get your argument on the front of newspapers, in the news bulletins and on social media.In the face of this onslaught, the UK government backtracked on plans to let AI firms use copyright-protected work without permission.The many artists who put their name to various letters and protests against the reforms to create a virtual red carpet, included: Sir Elton John, Sir Paul McCartney, Abba’s Björn Ulvaeus, the actor Julianne Moore and the Radiohead singer Thom Yorke.John had one of the most memorable soundbites, calling the government “absolute losers” who were on course to “rob young people of their legacy and their income”.Overall, the campaign was more sophisticated than just rounding up irritated celebrities. Beeban Kidron, a member of the upper house of the UK parliament and an award-winning film director, marshalled an effective political campaign against the proposals by pushing legislative amendments that would have spiked the plans. She also helped organise celebrity opposition.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailKidron says the campaign struck a chord with the public.“People care about the songs, books and pictures that influence the critical moments in their lives,” she says.Polling backed this up, with seven out of 10 adults in the UK supporting the payment of royalties to copyright holders whose work had been used to train AI models.The Australian prime minister should take heed, Kidron says.“Albanese has been a leader in standing up to tech. He should not squander his reputation by selling Australian creatives down the river.”The campaign against copyright reform also benefited from the ingenuity of an industry that knows how to grab people’s attention.

articles.title: Serbia’s populist president Aleksandar Vučić resigns to run for prime minister
articles.excerpt: Serbia’s populist president, Aleksandar Vučić, has resigned to pursue an attempt to become prime minister in an early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests.Vučić’s second presidential term would otherwise end in May next year. He is banned by the constitution from seeking a third term and said he was resigning to lead his rightwing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) in the 25 October ballot.The governing populists face a major challenge from a youth-backed movement that led protests triggered by a train station canopy collapse in November 2024 that killed 16 people in the northern city of Novi Sad.University students demanded accountability for the tragedy. Their struggle for justice and against corruption has grown into a strong movement that will attempt to oust the SNS after 14 years in power. Vučić has been either prime minister or president for the past 12 years.“I am resigning the duty of the president of the republic,” Vučić said, reading the text of his resignation.The ballot in October will be held against a backdrop of high political tensions as Vučić’s populists seek to remain in office despite widespread discontent. His decision to run for prime minister is seen as an attempt to retain a top position and boost his party’s chances against the student movement.Vučić supporters light flares outside the presidency in Belgrade after his resignation. Photograph: Đorđe Kojadinović/ReutersVučić has toured the country in recent weeks with live coverage on pro-government media.

articles.title: Pope Leo urges healing of ‘deep wounds’ before meeting child sexual abuse survivors in France
articles.excerpt: The pope has called on the Catholic church to heal “deep wounds” and “painful errors”, before a meeting survivors of child sexual abuse as he continues his four-day visit to France.Addressing a crowd in a large field near the Catholic shrine of Lourdes on Sunday, Pope Leo XIV called on the church to reckon with its past, without directly referencing sexual abuse scandals in France that affected at least 330,000 children over seven decades.“In order to heal the deep wounds, infidelities and ⁠painful errors that have occurred within [the church], we must humbly place ourselves under the Lord’s purifying gaze,” the first US pope told the estimated crowd of 150,000 people.Leo met seven survivors of child sexual abuse by French clergy privately on Sunday after leading an open-air morning mass at Lourdes, one of the most popular Catholic sites for pilgrims and reputed as a place of healing.The survivors said the pope had listened to them, was informed of their cases and said more work was needed to respond to the scandal.Five of the seven held a press conference in Lourdes. Jean-Marie Delbos said he never thought the day would come when he would meet a pope. He asked Leo to bless a photo of his grandmother, which he did. “It was extraordinary,” he said.Pope Leo celebrates a mass in Lourdes. Photograph: Remo Casilli/ReutersDuring a homily to the faithful, the pope also attacked medically assisted dying as immoral “false compassion” in a staunch articulation of the Catholic church’s teaching that all human life must be defended from conception until natural death.After years of debate, France formally adopted legislation last month allowing incurably ill adults the right to “aid in dying”, joining a small number of countries with similar laws, including Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Canada.The pope said: “It is impossible to regard causing death as something normal.

articles.title: Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would have curbed Nato cooperation
